title: Multiply & divide decimals
examples: When I multiply two decimals, do I count the places?
How do I divide by a number that has a decimal point?
Should I move the decimal point when dividing?

explain.say: Today we will learn to multiply and divide decimals. It is important to know the rules for both.
First, when multiplying decimals, you ignore the points. You multiply the numbers as if they were whole numbers.
Next, you count the total number of decimal places in the numbers you multiplied. This count tells you where to put the final point.

items: Move decimal to make it whole.

explain.say: For example, two point three times four point five has two places total. You multiply to get one point three and the point is placed after two digits.
Now for dividing by a decimal. You must make the divisor a whole number first. You do this by moving the decimal point.

items: Move decimal to make it whole.

faq.q: Do I move the decimal point when dividing by a decimal?
faq.a: Yes, you must make the number you are dividing by a whole number. You move the decimal point in both numbers the same amount.
asks: How do I fix the decimal in division?
Do I move the point in both numbers?

faq.q: If I multiply 0.5 by 100, what do I do?
faq.a: You move the decimal point two places to the right. This is the same as multiplying by one hundred.

faq.q: When multiplying, do I add up the decimal places?
faq.a: Yes, you count all the decimal places from every number you are multiplying. This total count tells you how many places to put the point back.

faq.q: What if the dividend is a decimal and the divisor is a whole number?
faq.a: You can treat it like normal division. You just place the decimal point in the answer directly above the dividend's point.
asks: Where does the point go in division?

faq.q: Is it always easier to multiply or divide decimals?
faq.a: Both require careful counting of decimal places. Remember to make the divisor whole when dividing by a decimal.

facts: When multiplying decimals, count the total decimal places.
To divide by a decimal, move the decimal point until the divisor is a whole number.
You must move the decimal point in both numbers the same amount when dividing.
The decimal point in the answer must have the correct number of places.

quiz.why: You multiply 12 times 3 to get thirty-six. Since there are two decimal places total, the answer is zero point thirty-six.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only count one decimal place total.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you count three decimal places total.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you forget to place the decimal point at all.

quiz.why: You move the point one place in both numbers, making it 96 divided by 3. The answer is thirty-two.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you move the decimal point too many places.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you add an extra zero unnecessarily.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you only move the decimal point in the dividend.

quiz.why: You divide 415 by 5, which is eighty-three. Since there are two decimal places in the original number, the answer needs two decimal places.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to put the decimal point in the answer.
wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly carries over the last digit from the division.
wrong.3: This mistake adds an extra zero at the end which is unnecessary.
